terms.definition: A protective package containing a baby plant (embryo) and its stored food, which can grow into a new plant.
terms.function: Can germinate and grow into a new plant.
terms.whyItMatters: Seeds are how flowering plants make the next generation and spread.

terms.definition: The tough outer layer of a seed that protects the embryo and its food.
terms.function: Shields the embryo until the seed germinates.
terms.whereItIs: The outer shell of the seed.
terms.whyItMatters: It lets the seed survive until conditions are right to grow.

terms.definition: The tiny baby plant that is inside a seed.
terms.function: It grows into the new plant at germination.
terms.whereItIs: Tucked inside the seed's stored food.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the living part of the seed that can start a new plant.

terms.definition: The process by which a seed begins to grow into a new plant after getting water, warmth, and air.
terms.function: Turns a resting seed into a growing seedling.
terms.whereItIs: Happens where the seed lands in a good spot.
terms.whyItMatters: It is what turns seeds into the plants all around us.
